claims: Optical instruments use prisms made of glass or other transparent materials.
Prisms are important components of instruments that investigate the colors of light.
Preserve telescope, periscope and other-device uses.
n74_requirements.SCI_limits: Do not convert these uses into a claim that every prism in every instrument necessarily operates by total internal reflection.

claims: Figure 160 is a section of the glass prism perpendicular to its lateral edges.
The described traversing ray refracts at both OA and OB.
The angle between those interfaces is the prism refracting angle phi; preserve the bold concept.
Deviation angle theta depends on prism angle phi, material refractive index n and incidence angle alpha.
SCI_limits: The two-refraction statement concerns the described transmitted path, not every possible incident ray.
A modern clarification may identify the surrounding medium and angle conventions, but must be distinguished from source wording.
No exact source diagram geometry, point locations or ray counts can be certified in this zero-image review.

claims: Optical instruments commonly use glass prisms with an isosceles right-triangle section.
Their described application relies on the glass critical angle being less than 45 degrees.
All three described figure configurations use total internal reflection.
Figure 161 turns the beam through 90 degrees; preserve the periscope use.
Figure 162 turns the beam direction through 180 degrees; preserve the prism-binocular use.
Figure 163 interchanges upper and lower rays emerging from an optical instrument, including the converse.
SCI_limits: The relevant critical angle is for glass to air, not an unconditional property of glass independent of the second medium.
Use of a 45-degree internal incidence requires the glass-to-air critical angle to be strictly less than 45 degrees; equality is the grazing boundary, not the strict-greater condition.
The text must not assert that an arbitrary glass prism or arbitrary placement in water satisfies the same condition.
Keep the 90-degree turn, 180-degree reversal and ray-order interchange distinct; do not substitute one for another or infer an unobserved whole-image transformation.
No figure-body PASS follows from checking these textual relationships.

prose.text: 在光学仪器中，常常要利用由玻璃或其它透明材料制成的三棱镜。这样的棱镜是研究光的颜色的仪器的最重要部件。它应用在望远镜、潜望镜和许多其它装置中。
图160所示的是平面玻璃棱镜的与侧棱垂直的截面。光线在棱镜中折射两次：在交界面$OA$和$OB$上。两个交界面之间的角$\varphi$叫做**棱镜的折射角**。光线的偏向角$\theta$取决于棱镜的折射角$\varphi$、棱镜材料的折射率$n$及入射角$\alpha$。

在光学仪器中，常常利用底面是等腰直角三角形的玻璃棱镜。它的应用是基于对玻璃的全反射的临界角小于$45^\circ$。所以在图161、162、163表示的各情况中，都发生全反射。在图161中，棱镜使光束偏转了$90^\circ$，这在潜望镜中是必需的。在棱镜双目望远镜中发生的是如图162所示的光路的情况：光束的方向变化了$180^\circ$。图163所示的是利用棱镜改变从某一光学仪器中射出的光线的次序，上面的光线变为下面的，以及反之。
